text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singaporeans can expect better government and public services when whole civil service goes autonomous next month, Finance Minister Richard Hu says.

- Minister of State for Defence Matthias Yao, who is also Singapore Armed Forces Recreation Association (SAFRA) President, reveals two big celebrations in store for public as part of this year's National Day, coinciding with SAFRA'S 25th anniversary.
- Singapore and United States sign landmark open skies agreement lifting all restrictions on operations of both countries' airlines, giving passengers more choice in flights and cheaper airfares.
- Three elderly sisters who claimed that they were tricked into selling three-storey house agree to settle matter outside court.
- One out of five Central Provident Fund investors make profits in share deals last year.
- Bank Negara assurances on bankers to honour existing loans despite new lending limits restore confidence in local bourse, making local stock market rebound again.
- U.S. dollar tops 126 Japanese yen for first time since January 1993.
- Singapore Power gears up for coming battle with new independent power producers Tuas Power and Sembawang Projects Engineering Co.
- Half Singapore's Central Provident Fund money withdrawn for property purchases, amounting to between Singapore $60 billion and S$65 billion.
- Market value of Van der Horst investments exceeds its book value by Singapore $180.73 million, about 300 percent.
- DBS Land and Temasek Holdings jointly embark on 366-room business class Merchant Court hotel project in Sydney.
- NatSteel surges to this year's peak of buying 3.5 million shares at S$3.74.
